description: I am Nathaniel Otchie, an aspiring aerospace engineer from Ghana. I am building a weather-tracking glider from scavenged parts (Project KITE) to save local fishermen from deadly storms. I am looking for teammates to explore how AI, data, and aerospace tech can solve environmental and climate challenges. Coders, designers, and storytellers welcome. Let's use space tech to protect vulnerable communities on Earth.
summary: Mission Architect 3D is a browser game that teaches real space mission design. Players pick a mission, then choose difficulty, launch vehicle, propulsion, power and instruments. They watch crews and a crane assemble an SLS-class rocket in a hangar, then fly the mission with real orbital physics. The game uses the rocket equation (Δv = Isp × g₀ × ln(m₀/m_f)) and two-body orbital motion, so every design choice changes what the mission can achieve. Players can rotate and zoom full 3D models of the launch stack, an Orion-style spacecraft and satellites. Each mission has its own colour and a live preview. Two modes serve everyone: Astronaut simulation for full control and Learner for plain-language guidance. It needs no install, so it works in classrooms and outreach events.
details: What it does: players select a mission, configure the vehicle, assemble it in a busy assembly hangar, and fly it with manual burns, timing, docking and landing. How it works: Δv = Isp × g₀ × ln(m₀/m_f), plus two-body orbital integration under Earth gravity. Benefits: it makes mission trade-offs visible and playable for students and beginners. Impact: classroom and outreach use with a single link. Tools: HTML, JavaScript, a custom canvas 3D renderer, and the browser’s built-in speech for mission voices. Creativity: every mission has its own colour and a live preview, and crews, cranes and 3D models bring the hangar to life. Factors considered: accuracy (NASA reference sizes), accessibility (Learner mode) and no-install access.
